Head_and_Face: Eyes are large, golden-brown, and protruding, positioned dorsolaterally on the head.
Large tympanum (eardrum) visible as a circular membrane behind the eye; in males, significantly larger than the eye.
Males exhibit a yellow throat during breeding season.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is robust and broad-headed.
Skin is smooth and moist with variable coloration from olive-green to brown dorsally with irregular dark mottling.
Ventral surface is white to yellowish with grey mottling.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Hind limbs are extremely long and muscular with fully webbed feet; webbing extends to the tips of all toes.
Forelimbs are shorter with unwebbed digits.

Head_and_Face: Eyes are large and protruding with golden or copper irises.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is slender.
Skin coloration is typically bright green but varies by species to include brown, yellow, or patterned forms.
Some species exhibit lateral stripes or dorsal markings.
Skin texture is smooth and slightly granular.
Many species have a white or cream ventral surface.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Most distinctive feature is enlarged adhesive toe pads (suckers) on the tips of all digits.
Hind limbs are long with partial webbing between toes; forelimbs are slender.

Head_and_Face: Head is broad and flattened with small, protruding eyes positioned dorsolaterally.
No external tympanum is visible.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is compact and toad-like.
Coloration is dark brown to black with mottled patterning.
Skin is rough and warty with small tubercles distributed across the dorsal surface.
Ventral surface is pale grey to white.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Hind limbs are moderately long with partially webbed feet; toes lack adhesive pads.
Forelimbs are short and stout.
Male has a tail-like copulatory organ (post-anal appendage).

Head_and_Face: Head is large and broad with a massive, hooked beak.
Eyes are small and dark.
Body_and_Plumage: Carapace (upper shell) is heart-shaped when viewed from above, reddish-brown to dark brown with a smooth, glossy surface.
Carapace has five vertebral scutes down the midline and four pairs of costal scutes on each side.
Plastron (lower shell) is cream to yellowish with a smooth surface.
Skin is scaly and grey-brown on exposed surfaces.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Front flippers are long and paddle-like with a single claw on each.
Rear flippers are shorter and used for steering.
No ability to retract head into shell.

Head_and_Face: Head is large with a distinctive notched upper jaw creating a double-pointed appearance.
Eyes are small and dark.
Body_and_Plumage: Carapace lacks hard bony scutes; covered in thick, leathery, oily skin with seven longitudinal ridges (keels).
Carapace coloration is dark grey to black with scattered white or pale spots.
Plastron is similarly leathery with five longitudinal ridges.
Skin is dark grey with a smooth, rubbery texture.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Front flippers are extremely long and narrow relative to body size, proportionally the longest of any sea turtle.
Rear flippers are short.
No ability to retract head into shell.

Head_and_Face: Head is relatively large with a pointed snout and small eyes positioned laterally.
Body_and_Plumage: Carapace is high-domed and oval, dark brown to black with a smooth, slightly glossy surface.
Carapace has three longitudinal keels in juveniles that become less prominent with age.
Plastron is small and yellowish with two hinges allowing partial closure.
Skin is grey to brown with a rough, scaly texture.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet and sharp claws.
Tail is short and thick.
No ability to fully retract into shell due to small plastron.

Head_and_Face: Head is moderately sized with a pointed snout and small eyes.
Skin coloration is grey to olive with distinctive striped or spotted patterning on the head and neck.
Body_and_Plumage: Carapace is oval and moderately domed with a smooth surface.
Coloration varies from brown to olive with concentric growth rings visible on each scute.
Some species exhibit ornate patterning with yellow or orange markings on dark scutes.
Plastron is large and hinged, enabling partial closure.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Limbs are moderately long with webbed feet and sharp claws.
Tail is short.
Skin texture is smooth with fine scales.

Head_and_Face: Head is moderately sized with a pointed snout and small eyes.
Skin coloration is brown to grey with orange, yellow, or red markings on the head, neck, and limbs.
Body_and_Plumage: Carapace is high-domed and oval, dark brown to black with variable yellow, orange, or radiating markings on each scute.
Surface texture is smooth with concentric growth rings.
Plastron is yellow to brown with dark markings.
Most distinctive feature is the hinged plastron that can close completely against the carapace.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Limbs are stout and elephantine (columnar) with non-webbed feet and curved claws.
Tail is short.
Skin texture is rough and scaly.

Head_and_Face: Eyes are large with vertical slit pupils adapted for nocturnal vision.
Movable eyelids are present (unlike most geckos which have a fixed transparent spectacle).
Body_and_Plumage: Body is slender.
Coloration is pale grey, pink, or cream with 4-6 broad, dark brown to black bands running from the neck to the tail base.
Bands are sharply demarcated and evenly spaced.
Skin is smooth and granular with fine, bead-like scales.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Limbs are slender with five digits; toes lack adhesive lamellae.
Digits have small claws.
Tail is cylindrical and slightly flattened, capable of autotomy; regenerated tail is smooth and lacks banding.

Head_and_Face: Head is large and triangular with a prominent dewlap (loose skin fold) hanging from the throat.
Eyes are large with round pupils and golden irises.
A large circular subtympanic shield (scale) is present below the tympanum.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is robust.
Coloration is bright green in juveniles, becoming darker green to greyish-green in adults with broad black bands on the body and tail.
Row of enlarged, spine-like scales running from the nape along the midline of the back to the tail base, forming a serrated crest.
Skin is covered in small, granular scales with larger, plate-like scales on the head.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Limbs are long and muscular with five clawed digits on each foot.
Tail is laterally compressed and longer than body, used for balance and defense.
